Team — drafting notes below and attaching a short legal memo (legal_note_indemnity.txt). Key points: 

- Custody/Notice: propose a split-draft clause: Redwood will have the right to assume defense for third-party claims alleging infringement of Redwood-owned model IP or core infra. Customer retains right to assume defense for claims tied to Customer Data or Customer-provided prompts/configurations. If both are implicated, parties will confer and, failing agreement within 10 business days, Redwood will assume defense with reservation of rights.

- Escrow / Insurance: propose escrow activation at USD 250,000. The order of recovery: (1) direct insurance proceeds (primary insurer for the party defending), (2) escrow, (3) direct indemnitor funds. To address Zephyr's concern about insurance delays, include a short-circuit remedy: if insurer fails to materially respond within 45 days, escrow may be accessed with notice to the insurer.

- Export control / sanctioned content carveout: include explicit carveouts for claims arising from Customer's export-restricted data or acts in violation of export laws — those should be Customer-responsibility.

I'll paste suggested contract snippets into the shared Drive doc. Once Ben confirms commercial acceptability we'll send to Samantha and Marc as tracked changes.

Samantha / Marc — thanks for the quick turn. We discussed internally and propose the following compromise for the MSA redline exchange: 

1) Custody: Customer (Zephyr) may assume defense for claims that solely concern Customer Data or Customer-provided prompts/configs. Redwood will retain the right to assume defense for claims alleging infringement of Redwood models, tooling, or services. Where claims implicate both, Redwood may assume defense after 10 business days if parties cannot agree.

2) Escrow trigger: USD 250,000 with an insurer-first recovery waterfall and a 45-day insurer response backstop enabling limited escrow access with notice.

3) If Zephyr strongly requires a $200k trigger, Redwood will accept it only if Zephyr (a) increases the order-form liability cap by 10%, or (b) signs an explicit dataset-origin warranty and carveout that limits exposure for training-set-origin claims.

Next steps: If Zephyr agrees to the above, we will prepare a tracked-change MSA redline reflecting Kimberly's snippets and send it by tomorrow for your review. Ben will continue to coordinate commercial tradeoffs if you pursue option (a). We will prepare a DocuSign envelope once redlines are accepted: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/1234567890

Appreciate the partnership — aiming to get this across the finish line next week.
